units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on II Kings 6:25">Targ. II Kings VI, 25</cite>.—[<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Jeremiah 8:20">Targ. Jer. VIII, 20</cite> <he>שלים קִבָּא</he>, read with ed. Lag. <cite ref="S01120"><he>קִצָּא</he></cite>.]—

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 29a:3">Snh. 29ᵃ</cite> <he>אטו בק׳ דקירא וכ׳</he> am I stuck to you by (a gift of) a Kab of wax?, i.e. am I not free to form my own opinion? <cite ref="Yevamot 17a:9">Yeb. 17ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="C01092"><he>גַּנְדַּר</he> I</cite>.

<cite ref="Pesachim 113a:7">Pes. 113ᵃ</cite> <he>ק׳ מארעא ולא כורא מאיגרא</he> better a Kab from the ground, than a Kor from the roof, i.e. better a small profit at home, than a large one from abroad (for which you look out anxiously from your roof-top).
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 27a:21">Snh. 27ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>ק׳ דחושלא</he> a Kab of peeled barley; a. fr.—Pl. <he>קַבִּין</he>; <cite ref="S00047"><he>קַבַּיָּיא</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Challah 2:3:3">Y. Ḥall. II, 58ᵈ</cite> top <he>ק׳ באתריהון רובעיא אזדרעון</he> (read <he>אתערעון</he>, v. <cite ref="P01411"><he>עֲרַע</he> I</cite>) the Kabs (measures) in their place were enlarged by one fourth.—
<cite ref="Esther Rabbah 1:1">Esth. R. to I, 1</cite> the world is shaped <he>כאפי קַבָּאֵי</he> (prob. to be read: <he>קביא</he>) like the outside of round measures.
